Kiyosaki Warns Of a Crash Bigger Than 2008
The "Rich Dad Poor Dad" author blamed the Federal Reserve and big investment banks like
BlackRock
for eroding savers’ wealth through constant money printing, noting that the Fed and Treasury print roughly $1 trillion every 90 days while U.S. debt has climbed to $49 trillion.

He pointed back to 2008, recalling his own on-air prediction that Lehman Brothers would collapse, and said the derivatives market behind today’s risks is measured in the quadrillions rather than the trillions that nearly broke the economy then.

"This crash we are just now sliding into is much bigger than 2008. Possibly a global depression," Kiyosaki wrote, adding that AI-driven layoffs, including VW’s cut of 100,000 jobs, and unrest in Europe are already showing the strain.
He added "the big print is about to begin" as governments move to paper over the damage.
Why He’s Still Buying Bitcoin And Ethereum
Kiyosaki noted he’s sticking with real gold, silver, Bitcoin and Ethereum rather than ETFs, along with real estate and oil, as a hedge against that currency debasement.
If his call turns out right, those holdings could push him into the "ultra rich" category, he added.
Benzinga

that Kiyosaki already saw Bitcoin’s selloff as a buying opportunity, pointing to its fixed supply of 21 million coins, with roughly 20 million already mined, as proof it behaves unlike traditional money.
Not Everyone Thinks The Bottom Is In
Veteran trader Peter Brandt struck a more cautious tone in that same coverage, noting that every prior Bitcoin bull-market phase has ended with a correction of at least 75% from its peak.
Brandt also pointed to analysis from Kevin Capital flagging a potential bottom near the $60,600-$56,600 "golden pocket," with the $57,177 level on the 200-period EMA as another zone worth watching.
